queries.query: Eckhart's sermon on sanctification: the heart must stand empty of every creature and image, like a writing surface that must be blank before anything new can be set down on it
queries.note: The white-tablet analogy in the sermon on sanctification; 'wipe the tablet clean', 'vacant of all other things' paraphrased away; 'Eckhart' and the sermon topic kept as reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: Eckhart preaching that God bears his Son in the soul whether a person is willing or not, asleep or awake, just as the ground cannot escape the sky pouring down on it
queries.note: The birth of the Son in the soul from the sermon on the angel's greeting; 'the earth cannot flee from heaven', 'rains its influence', 'stamps its impress' paraphrased away.

queries.query: Eckhart preaching on 'the kingdom of God is near': the kingdom lies within us, and God waits inside, prepared and friendly, while we linger outside, estranged and unprepared
queries.note: The 'God is ready, we are unready' antitheses closing the sermon on the nearness of the kingdom, paraphrased into indirect statement; the sermon's scripture text kept as a reader-honest anchor. First nameless draft ('God stands prepared and close at hand while people remain distant') missed top-15 entirely — no christian_mysticism at all.

queries.query: if God is unchanging and already knows everything, what is the point of asking him for things in prayer
queries.note: Eckhart's answer that God foresaw all prayers from eternity; petitionary prayer under divine immutability is answered across traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: why is suffering held to be the fastest road to spiritual perfection
queries.note: 'Nothing is sharper than suffering, nothing is sweeter than to have suffered'; redemptive suffering is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
